title: Power Pages: security agent in design studio configures authentication and authorisation

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: The feature description and roadmap dates are supported, but the briefing incorrectly presents a site-chatbot publishing setting as a gate for the maker security agent. It also asserts unverified access and governance rules, and its scan automation entry is an operation name rather than a usable API call.

claims.claim: The roadmap item is in development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; changes
claims.claim: General availability is targeted for November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives April CY2026 as the preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "April CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only cloud listed on the roadmap; sovereign clouds are not listed.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The capability is enabled automatically for admins, makers and marketers, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: The publishing setting is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Tenant settings > Publish Copilots with AI features.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Manage. ... In the Manage pane, select Tenant settings. ... Publish Copilots with AI features

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the named publishing setting is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Publish Copilots with AI features tenant setting PowerShell Set-TenantSettings api. Opened tenant-settings and list-tenantsettings; the possible enableOpenAiBotPublishing property is explicitly unused, not a documented working equivalent.

claims.claim: Power Pages AI settings are at Power Platform admin center > Copilot Hub > Power Pages > Settings.
claims.quote: To view or update these settings, navigate to Copilot hub > Power Pages > Settings in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for environment-level Power Pages maker AI settings is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Copilot hub maker AI features environment settings PowerShell API disable; Power Pages Copilot environment API settings disable maker. Opened copilot-hub and admin-api; PowerShell references concern tenant settings, not this environment control.

claims.claim: The Run scan section is in the Security workspace of Power Pages design studio.
claims.quote: You can view the scan report summary by returning to the Run scan section of the Security workspace.

claims.claim: Start Deep Scan / Get Security Scan Report (powerpages namespace) is the API call for scan automation.
claims.quote: Searched: opened admin-api and the linked start-deep-scan and get-security-scan-report references. The printed text names operations but provides no HTTP method, endpoint or API version and is not an executable call.
claims.fix: Replace the call with POST https://api.powerplatform.com/powerpages/environments/{environmentId}/websites/{id}/scan/deep/start?api-version=2024-10-01 and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/power-platform/powerpages/websites/start-deep-scan. If showing report retrieval, give a separate GET https://api.powerplatform.com/powerpages/environments/{environmentId}/websites/{id}/scan/deep/getLatestCompletedReport?api-version=2024-10-01 with its get-security-scan-report reference.

claims.claim: A dedicated whole-security-agent switch has no documented UI or API.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent disable switch tenant environment; Power Pages security agent disable. Opened security-agent, faq-security-agent, copilot-hub and admin-api. FAQ mentions toggling individual use cases, not a whole-agent switch or its path/API.

claims.claim: Publish Copilots with AI features gates all Power Pages AI features, including the maker security agent.
claims.quote: Chat agent (site Copilot) specific setting: If the setting for “Publish bots with AI” is disabled at the tenant level, admins are unable to configure site Copilot at the environment level.
claims.fix: Remove this setting as a prerequisite or gate for the security agent. If retaining the row as background, label it a site-chatbot publishing control and explicitly state that Microsoft has not confirmed applicability to the maker security agent.

claims.claim: The security agent inherits the Copilot hub's environment-level governance.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent disable enable governance; Power Pages Copilot hub maker AI features environment settings. Opened security-agent, copilot-hub and copilot-governance. None explicitly puts Security agent under Studio Copilot or confirms this inheritance.
claims.fix: Keep the documented general Power Pages maker-AI control, but add a note: 'General Power Pages AI control; Microsoft has not confirmed that it governs Security agent.' Replace the categorical inheritance statement with that qualification.

claims.claim: Who can edit the site determines who can use the security agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent role access edit permissions; Power Pages security agent permissions edit. Opened security-agent and faq-security-agent; neither defines site-edit permission as the sufficient access rule for the agent.
claims.fix: Replace 'Governed by who can edit the site' with 'The feature documentation does not specify the roles or privileges required to use the agent; confirm access in a test environment.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A separate licence for this security-agent capability is not stated, so its licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent licensing; Power Pages security agent preview licensing pricing credits. Opened security-agent and faq-security-agent and read licensing FAQ search excerpts; no security-agent licence requirement was stated.

claims.claim: No separate security-agent meter or credit charge is stated in the roadmap or preview documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent credits pricing; Power Pages security agent preview licensing pricing credits. Read the roadmap, security-agent, faq-security-agent and licensing search results; none states a security-agent meter or credit rate.

claims.claim: General-availability pricing and any consumption model for this capability are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages security agent credits pricing; Power Pages security agent licensing. Read security-agent, faq-security-agent and Power Pages licensing search results; no GA pricing or consumption model specific to Security agent was stated.

claims.claim: Power Pages licensing continues to apply to the underlying site.
claims.quote: As you work on projects and need to establish permanent sites that don't expire, you can apply Power Pages subscriptions and convert websites from trial to production.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/go-live/assign-licensing for the underlying site's licensing, without implying it establishes the security agent's separate entitlement.

claims.claim: The older tenant-level governance experience under Resources is being deprecated in favour of Copilot hub.
claims.quote: The tenant-level governance configuration feature is now deprecated. ... Going forward, all governance settings for Copilot features must be managed through the Copilot hub.
claims.fix: Point the deprecation link to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/copilot-hub#admin-experience, which states the deprecation. Clarify that the older control covered site-user AI experiences and expressly excluded maker experiences.

claims.claim: Administrators can initiate the Power Pages deep security scan from the admin center's security pages.
claims.quote: Site-specific details, including the scan status, scan score (number of passed/failed checks), if the scan is completed, a view of the scan results, and an option to initiate the scan.

claims.claim: The security-agent system includes security scanning.
claims.quote: It combines scheduled vulnerability scanning, real-time traffic anomaly detection, and guided remediation
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/faq-security-agent and distinguish the broader agent system's scheduled scanning from the chat assistant's documented ability to analyse scan findings; avoid implying a chat command to launch a scan is documented.

claims.claim: The Power Pages admin API exposes deep-scan initiation and report retrieval.
claims.quote: Get Security Scan Report ... Get deep scan report for a Power Pages website. ... Start Deep Scan ... Start deep scan for a Power Pages website.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review Security workspace access, web roles and table permissions without corresponding control rows.
claims.quote: Confirm which roles can open the Security workspace. ... Review web roles and table permissions after agent-driven changes. The table contains publishing, AI feature settings, scans and a missing dedicated switch.
claims.fix: Add rows for site-maker/Security workspace access, web roles and table permissions. For web roles and table permissions, use https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/getting-started/use-security-workspace and its linked configuration references; keep unconfirmed agent-specific access requirements explicit.

claims.claim: The low cost rating covers known admin and maker review time while feature-specific licensing remains unpublished.
claims.quote: Review all proposed configuration changes before approving write actions. ... Validate and deploy approved changes using your organization's standard ALM process.
